A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe the same GenPercept work, and their supplied text, equations, tables and figures are readable. However, v1 refers to supplementary DIS comparisons that are absent from its supplied PDF, limiting comparison of that material. The principal method, experiments and revisions remain assessable.

before.justification: v1 reports original GenPercept experiments on depth, surface normals, segmentation, matting and human pose, together with component and training-data ablations.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results and extensive adaptation ablations, with additional empirical comparisons and qualitative results in its appendices.

M1.justification: The one-step backbone and optional decoder mechanism remain, but task-specific learning changes substantially. v3 adds disparity prediction, uses MSE/scale-shift-invariant/gradient depth losses instead of v1's VNL/HDN/MSE/L1 combination, and adds image-angular supervision for normals. Colormap segmentation changes from latent-space supervision to pixel-wise MSE. These revise outputs and objectives beyond merely documenting the existing architecture.

E1.justification: v3 adds ScanNet depth evaluation, Sintel normal evaluation, and Taskonomy/Cityscapes training for the data-quality comparison (Tables 5–7). Appendix E.6 additionally reports MHP pose experiments. The original COCO pose coverage is retained in Appendix C, rather than removed.

E2.justification: The depth benchmark gains DepthAnything, DepthAnything v2, Metric3D v2, Marigold, GeoWizard and DepthFM. Normal comparisons replace FrameNet, VPLNet, TiltedSN and Bae et al. (2021) with Omnidata variants, Metric3D v2, DSINE and GeoWizard. Matting adds HATT, SHM and MODNet. Conversely, v1's DINOv2 depth and semantic-segmentation comparisons disappear. P3M becomes P3M-Net with the same comparator scores.

E3.justification: Default ablations change from Hypersim-only training at resolution 768 and batch size 16 (v1 Section 3.5) to 90:10 Hypersim/Virtual KITTI sampling at 480×640 and batch size 32 (v3 Appendix D). Normal evaluation drops RMSE and adds 5° and 7.5° thresholds. v3 also introduces average ranks across depth metrics. These are substantive reported protocol changes.

E4.justification: v3 expands the noise/component studies to test both noise forms, multi-resolution noise, image-level losses, prompts, timesteps, LoRA ranks and synthetic versus real training data (Tables 1–5). It adds qualitative ablation and semantic failure examples. Conversely, v1's training-data-volume sweep, PixArt and VAE-encoder tests, and explicit ensemble/runtime analysis are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Inference ensembles and discussion of diffusion stochasticity do not establish statistical uncertainty reporting; both versions principally report point estimates.

E6.justification: v3 substantially replaces and extends geometry and ablation results under revised settings. DIS overall maxFβ changes from 0.840 to 0.863 (v1 Table 4; v3 Table 8); matting SAD/MSE change from 12.44/0.0037 to 12.77/0.0027 (v1 Table 5; v3 Table 10). These are revised reported outcomes under changed training, not controlled same-setting improvements. GenPercept's semantic mIoU and COCO pose scores are retained.

T1.justification: The diffusion formulations and beta-equals-one derivation in v1 Section 2, Equations 1–8, are retained in v3 Appendix A. No new theorem, proof or substantive formal derivation is introduced. The expanded empirical explanations do not change this mathematical content.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds simple diffusion-backbone initialization and transfer using limited target data. v3 makes systematic identification of effective adaptation choices a principal contribution, with headline findings about annotation quality, stochasticity and image-level supervision. It emphasizes dense perception while retaining GenPercept's transfer claim and moving pose evidence to the appendix.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations for LoRA's limitations, annotation quality and supervision effects on detail, and depth-versus-disparity tradeoffs. It explicitly qualifies semantic generalization with failures on unseen cats and cars (Figure 4). Meanwhile, v1's MAE/CLIP/CoCa representation-learning discussion and interpretations of the removed data-volume and PixArt experiments disappear.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository pointer and documents sampling ratios, noise/ensemble defaults, prompt strings, LoRA ranks and MMPose rendering. It omits v1's explicit learning-rate decay, DIS/matting normalization and clipping instructions, and runtime/memory measurements. These change reproducibility documentation within an otherwise retained implementation framework; the link alone does not establish external code availability.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts from broad foundation-model transfer and NLP/pretraining analogies toward identifying unresolved diffusion-adaptation choices. Marigold and DMP remain but become central reference points. GeoWizard, DepthFM, DepthAnything, Metric3D v2 and newer inverse-rendering work substantially expand the contemporary context, while much of the earlier NLP, DINOv2 and representation-learning discussion is removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. The method-first narrative becomes a preliminary overview followed by question-driven analyses and explicit findings before task experiments. Detailed formulations move to Appendix A, human pose moves to Appendix C, and implementation and supplementary results receive separate appendices. This is substantial narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: Figure 2 becomes a multi-panel visualization of noise forms, schedules and predictions; Figure 4 gains generalization and failure examples. Geometry tables expand to additional datasets, methods and training-sample columns, while the semantic table loses baseline and architecture columns. Boxed findings and extensive appendix comparison grids are added, alongside relocation of the pose table and figure.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the justification for adaptation choices: Table 1 investigates both stochastic and deterministic noise schedules, and Tables 2–5 isolate supervision, conditioning and fine-tuning choices that v1 examined less fully. Broader geometry comparisons and explicit semantic failure cases improve the assessment of applicability. Removing DINOv2 comparisons, data-scaling evidence and measured runtime/memory results loses useful support, but the stronger investigation of the central design questions provides a substantial net quality gain.
